## Overview

This dossier synthesizes information from the [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) [Economic Survey](../document-types/economic-survey.qmd) (2025-04-28), the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) [Debt Sustainability Monitor](../document-types/debt-sustainability-monitor.qmd) (2026-02-12), the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) [Economic Forecast](../document-types/economic-forecast.qmd) (2026-05-21), and the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) [Country Report](../document-types/country-report.qmd) (2026-06-03). The evidence highlights a slowdown in economic growth driven by structural productivity stagnation and external shocks, alongside a shift from fiscal surplus to deficit. Structural challenges include housing affordability, pension sustainability risks due to demographic aging, and low long-term growth potential. The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) classifies medium-term debt sustainability risks as low to medium, though long-term fiscal gaps are significant.

## Economic

### C1\* Growth ([Growth](../parameters/growth.qmd))

#### C1-E Broken or dominated sample

[No evidence in the sources yet.]{.no-evidence}

#### C1-T Structural break in trend

- **C1-T, structural break in trend**: Real GDP growth slowed to 1.1% in 2020–2025, significantly below the historical mean of 4.5% in 2000–2007 and 2.5% in 2010–2019. Medium-term forecasts project growth of 1.6% in 2026 and 2.0% in 2027, remaining below historical trends. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- **C1-T, structural break**: Real GDP growth is expected to accelerate to 1.6% in 2026 and 2.0% in 2027, supported by services exports. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 134" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 134">ⓘ</button>

#### C1-A1 Growth not thin-tailed or serially independent

[No evidence in the sources yet.]{.no-evidence}

#### C1-A2 Inherited competitiveness gap

- **C1-A2, inherited competitiveness gap**: Labor productivity has stagnated since the early 2010s, with labor productivity decreasing by 1.6% and total factor productivity falling by 1.8% on average per year between 2021 and 2025. The financial sector, accounting for around 25% of value added, shows negative productivity growth, pointing to diminishing efficiency gains. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, pp. 4, 12" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, pp. 4, 12">ⓘ</button>
- **[C1-A2, competitiveness gap]**: Unit labor costs increased by about 15% since the end of 2021, leading to an appreciation in the unit labor cost-based real effective exchange rate, although this has partially reversed as nominal wages in neighboring countries caught up <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 21" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 21">ⓘ</button>.
- **[C1\*, context]**: Measured labor productivity in [Luxembourg](../countries/luxembourg.qmd) is among the highest in the OECD, but growth has stagnated since 2010, driven by declining multi-factor productivity and slowing capital deepening <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 80-82" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 80-82">ⓘ</button>.

#### Other growth context

- **[C1\*, context]**: The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) projects real GDP growth to recover gradually, reaching 2.1% in 2025 and 2.3% in 2026, supported by easing financial conditions and a gradual recovery in the construction sector <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 9" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 9">ⓘ</button>.

## Fiscal

### C3\* Fiscal capacity and plan ([Fiscal Capacity](../parameters/fiscal-capacity.qmd))

#### C3-E Estimator fails or rests on one episode

[No evidence in the sources yet.]{.no-evidence}

#### C3-T History lags policy

- **C3-T, history lags policy**: [Luxembourg](../countries/luxembourg.qmd) was found not compliant with its medium-term fiscal-structural plan commitments in 2025. The annual deviation from the recommended net expenditure path was 1.3% of GDP, and the cumulative deviation was 0.6% of GDP. The general government balance turned to a deficit of 2.0% of GDP in 2025, after a surplus of 0.9% in 2024, driven by higher spending on defense, housing, and climate measures. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- **[C3-T, history lags policy]**: Under unchanged tax and spending policies, gross public debt would remain stable until the late 2040s but would rise rapidly thereafter due to aging-related expenditure, particularly pensions <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 27" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 27">ⓘ</button>.
- **C3-T, history lags policy**: The general government balance is forecast to remain in deficit, improving to -1.2% in 2026 and widening slightly to -1.5% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 135" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 135">ⓘ</button>
- **[C3-T, context]**: The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) recommends adopting a national net spending rule to anchor fiscal policy, replacing the obsolete EU-mandated medium-term objective <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 31, 46" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 31, 46">ⓘ</button>.

#### C3-A Default is chosen, not only suffered

[No evidence in the sources yet.]{.no-evidence}

#### Other fiscal context

- **C3\*, context**: Public debt is projected to increase from 26.5% of GDP in 2025 to 30.2% in 2027, mostly due to budget deficits and stock-flow adjustments. Risks to the fiscal plan include lower than projected economic growth and increasing spending pressures from aging and defense commitments. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, pp. 5, 37" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, pp. 5, 37">ⓘ</button>
- **C3\*, context**: The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) projects a structural primary surplus of 1.4% of GDP as of 2026. This is low compared with past fiscal performance. Ageing-related expenditure is projected to increase. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 197" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 197">ⓘ</button>
- **C3\*, context**: The S2 indicator points to high risk, requiring a 7.1 percentage point improvement, driven by ageing costs (7.8 pps). The S1 indicator points to medium risk, requiring a 2.0 percentage point effort. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 198" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 198">ⓘ</button>
- **[C3\*, context]**: [Luxembourg](../countries/luxembourg.qmd) has a history of prudent budget management, with gross public debt below 30% of GDP in 2023 and net government financial assets of about 50% of GDP <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 26" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 26">ⓘ</button>.
- **[C3\*, context]**: The fiscal stance is broadly neutral in 2025, but the [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) advises phasing out energy policy supports and accelerating consolidation from 2026 to rebuild fiscal buffers <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 27-28" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 27-28">ⓘ</button>.

## Debt

### R1\* Refinancing need ([Refinancing Need](../parameters/refinancing-need.qmd))

#### R1-E Components missing or distorted

- **R1-E, components missing**: The debt-to-GDP ratio is projected to increase to 30.2% by 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 135" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 135">ⓘ</button>

#### R1-T Financing behavior shifts

[No evidence in the sources yet.]{.no-evidence}

#### R1-A Part of the debt not exposed to the market

- **R1-A, context**: Risk-increasing factors relate to contingent liability risks from the private sector and changes in international financial regulations. Risk-mitigating factors include lengthening debt maturity, stable financing sources, euro denomination, and a positive net international investment position. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 198" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 198">ⓘ</button>

#### Other refinancing context

- **R1\*, context**: Gross general government debt stood at 26.5% of GDP at the end of 2025. Debt is expected to rise to 30.2% of GDP in 2027. The report notes that public investment remained high at 5.0% of GDP in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, p. 37" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, p. 37">ⓘ</button>
- **R1\*, context**: Gross financing needs were 3.6% of GDP in 2025. Debt is projected to remain stable at 20.1% of GDP by 2036. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20, 42" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 20, 42">ⓘ</button>
- **R1\*, context**: Gross financing needs are expected to decrease to around 3% of GDP on average over 2026-2027, reaching around 2% of GDP in 2036. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 197" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 197">ⓘ</button>
- **[R1\*, context]**: Gross public debt (Maastricht definition) was 24.9% of GDP in 2023 and is projected to remain low, at 23.5% in 2026 <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 9" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 9">ⓘ</button>.
- **[R1\*, context]**: Net financial debt was -48.2% of GDP in 2023, indicating strong net creditor position <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 7" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 7">ⓘ</button>.

## Institutions

### R6\* Backstop eligibility ([Backstop Eligibility](../parameters/backstop-eligibility.qmd))

#### Bright-line inputs

- **R6\*, context**: [Luxembourg](../countries/luxembourg.qmd) has been found not compliant with its fiscal commitments under the EU fiscal framework, with an annual and cumulative deviation of 1.3% and 0.6% of GDP respectively in 2025. The Council endorsed its medium-term fiscal-structural plan, which aims to keep the deficit well below 3% of GDP by 2029 and public debt below 60% of GDP. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>

### National institutions

- **[R6-A, context]**: The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) suggests enhancing the mandate of the national fiscal council to include long-term debt sustainability assessments and to monitor compliance with the new national fiscal rule <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 31, 46" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 31, 46">ⓘ</button>.

## Market Signals

- **Rollover pessimism**: The 10-year sovereign yield spread vs. German Bund is 29 basis points as of 31 December 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 199" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 199">ⓘ</button>

## Outlook Material

- **Housing and Labor Market**: High house prices and limited supply pose systemic risks. House prices in 2025 were 60% higher than a decade ago. The unemployment rate rose above the EU average for the first time since 2009, reaching 6.5% in 2025. Skills mismatches are significant, with macroeconomic skills mismatches rising to 34.4% in 2025, far above the EU average of 19.2%. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, pp. 5, 22" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, pp. 5, 22">ⓘ</button>
- **Pension Sustainability**: The pension system is projected to start running a deficit as of 2029 due to unfavorable demographic dynamics. The pay-as-you-go Pillar I reserve is projected to be entirely depleted by 2048. A 2025 pension reform increased contribution rates by 1.5 percentage points to 25.5% but is deemed insufficient to fully address structural sustainability issues or significantly increase the low participation rate of workers aged 55–64 (51.9% in 2025). <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, pp. 6, 39" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, pp. 6, 39">ⓘ</button>
- **Tax Planning**: Aggressive tax planning remains unaddressed. [Luxembourg](../countries/luxembourg.qmd) introduced a non-deductibility rule for interest and royalty payments, but its scope is limited. The country is identified as a conduit for capital flows, with net inward FDI stock 31 times larger than GDP. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, pp. 8, 45" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, pp. 8, 45">ⓘ</button>
- **[Pension Sustainability]**: The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) identifies the pension system's sustainability as a major long-term risk, projecting pension expenditure to rise from 9.4% of GDP in 2024 to 17.5% in 2070 without reform <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 54" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 54">ⓘ</button>.
- **[Climate Transition]**: The transition to green growth will have a net negative impact on the budget balance, estimated at around 2% of GDP by 2050, primarily due to lower fuel revenues <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 28, 30" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 28, 30">ⓘ</button>.
- **[Housing]**: Housing affordability remains low, with real house prices falling by about 20% since late 2022, but affordability deteriorating further due to higher interest rates <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 40" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 40">ⓘ</button>.
